pages.text: The trees would not fall to my fists. I tried until my knuckles split. This world doesn't reward stubbornness, only cleverness. So I sat by a river and looked at what lay around me: gravel, stone, grass and sticks.

Flint first. Gravel gives it up grudgingly. Struck against stone, flint splits into shards sharp enough to cut, if it doesn't shatter first. Most do. I learned patience before I learned anything else.

Two shards make a blade. A blade on a stick makes a knife, and with a knife the grass gives up its fibre. Fibre twists into string, and string binds a shard to a stick. That was my first hatchet. I nearly wept.
Planks came hardest. My hands could not make them, so I chopped them one log at a time, on a stump I made myself. With two planks, a frame and a blade I built a table. It was crooked. It was mine.
The tables in villages never worked for me; only the one I made myself. Keep it close. You'll need one again at the very end.
pages.title: Mark of the Stone Age
